question: In issue No 2/2023 of its Journal on ‘Migration policy and the EU’1, the Court of Auditors looks at a 2022 report published by the United Nations Human Rights Council (UNHRC). The report presents resettlement in a third country of refugees and forcibly displaced persons as a durable migration policy solution. It notes that the number of forcibly displaced persons has increased significantly. In 2022, at least 5.

7 million displaced persons returned to their places of origin – 8 % more than in the previous year. In the same year, 339 300 refugees returned to their countries of origin, while 114 300 refugees were resettled to a safe third country. 1.

Does the Commission agree with the UNHRC, which concluded that, despite the many challenges, some groups of refugees have been able to return to their home countries because lasting peace has been secured?
Will it step up efforts to help migrants return as quickly as possible to their own country, rather than encouraging them to come to the EU?
answer: Every year, the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees publishes its Global Trends report on forced displacement. These reports contain data about displaced people, including refugees returning home. The cited figures come from the 2022 Global Trends report (2) (p. 10). Most people who have been forced to flee wish to return home.

For them, if conditions of safety and dignity are met, voluntary return is the preferred ‘durable solution’ (3). Most third-country nationals come to the EU legally and they have a right to stay in the EU. Regarding those that do not have a right to stay, EU law requires that they return to their country of origin. In the past years, the Commission has invested significant efforts and funding in stepping up returns.

The Commission has worked on strengthening readmission cooperation with key countries of origin and, at the same time, on improving the return processes in Member States, reinforced by the efforts of the Return Coordinator and the High-Level Network on Return since 2022.

Return, readmission and sustainable reintegration are essential elements of the comprehensive migration policy put forward by the Pact on Migration and Asylum (4). Establishing an effective and common EU system for returns is a central goal of the Pact with focus on combining stronger structures inside the EU with more effective cooperation with third countries on return and readmission.
The Commission is working closely with Member States, EU Agencies and civil society to achieve this goal.
